2. The plaintiff instituted the suit challenging the notice dated 30.10.1983 asserting that suit land belonged to Alekjan Bibi whose name was recorded in C.S. and R.S. in Plot Nos. 42-44 and 55 in S.A. Khatian No. 364. The southern portion in the building was requisitioned by the Deputy Commissioner, Comilla excluding the third Schedule land and northern portion was requisitioned in Requisition Case No. 337 of 1988. On 24.12.1962 the land of second Schedule was sold to plaintiff who was in possession of third Schedule out of the second Schedule land. Defendant having illegally issued Memo dated 30.10.1983 for removing bamboo fancying from the northern portion of the second Schedule was constrained to file the suit. 

 3. The defendants, however, alleged that suit premises including third Schedule belonged to Alekjan Bibi and the C.S. Khatian was prepared in her name accordingly who sold the same to Rahatarunnessa and Swarez Kumar Gupta who in their turn sold to Tara Nath Rakshit who then sold to Upendra Prasad Roy on 27.4.1934. The building was requisitioned in R.C. No. 337 of 1948 and since then the allottees have been residing thereto. Government as well leased the same land to Anjuman-i-Mofidul Islam. The plaintiff filed the suit to grab the land as Upendra left for India resulting the suit land being vested and non-resident property. 

 "The plaintiffs adduced 3 witnesses and produced the original deed of sale Ext. 1. The same was exhibited without any objection by the defendants and as such the defendants cannot complain about the same any more. There is nothing to show that the document is spurious. The notice dated 30.10.83 itself shows that the plaintiff was in unlawful possession. The plaintiff produced an information report from the office of the vested and non-resident property dated 25.1.87 which shows that the property is question has  not been treated as vested and non-resident property by the office. The courts below found fault of producing with the certified copy of the porcha (FOR) showing the name of Alekjan Bibi. It is admitted that the land in question was recorded in the name of Alekjan Bibi in C.S. Khatian and it was recorded in S.A. Khatian accordingly on 20.3.83 Ext. B. But suddenly for the reason best known to the defendant that was cancelled on 30.5.85 P.Ws. 1, 2 and 3 said that they are in possession and until the deed is proved to be forged it is pressured that the document was executed by Alekjan Bibi and accordingly disputed land belongs to the plaintiff." 

 6. The aforesaid finding apart, both the Courts below concurrently found that the suit land originally belonged to Alekjan Bibi in whose name C.S. and R.S. Khatians stood. The Court of appeal below also found that "From the papers filed by the defendants it is seen that those papers are certified copies of same old deeds and from the same it is seen that Alekjan transferred the entire land of the suit plot to her daughter Golabjan in 1299 B.S. and by way successive transfers Upendra Prasad Roy acquired 30 decimals of land of suit plot it is also admitted that Govt. requisitioned the suit property. The plaintiff claims to have purchased the suit property from Alekjan in 1369 13:S. i.e. about 70 years after the transfer of the suit land by Alekjan to her daughter Golabjan. The story of such transaction appears to me to be very doubtful." The Court of appeal below also found that admittedly the defendants are in possession of the suit land by way of requisition so the defendants have no locus standi without getting his title and possession in the suit land declared by the competent Court to challenge the impugned notice dated 30.10.83 of the respondent No. 4.
